title: Autonomous escalation bridge: PD + Slack + trace snapshots + postmortem skeleton
creator: Anika Patel
description: Build an autonomous escalation bridge that synthesizes observability artifacts (trace snapshots, metric snippets, recent error logs) and automates incident creation and postmortem scaffolding across PagerDuty, Slack, and our documentation templates. The bridge should be usable by both Hosted API and Dedicated clusters and work with existing tracing hooks and metric pipelines.
background: We currently have ad-hoc workflows: alerts hit PagerDuty, on-call manually pastes links to traces/dashboards into Slack and a postmortem is created after manual triage. This causes slow MTTA/MTTR, inconsistent postmortem quality, and repeated manual effort. Recent incidents showed missing trace context when follow-ups were needed (see ENG-41204). This ticket ties observability snapshots to incident tooling to standardize the response flow.
acceptance_criteria: PagerDuty incidents created contain a stable link to an immutable trace snapshot + a short auto-generated summary (service, symptom, top span names)

A Slack channel and a pinned thread are auto-created for the incident with an interactive message that includes: links to trace snapshot, top metrics chart PNG, last 200 error logs, and buttons: 'Acknowledge', 'Attach Runbook', 'Create Postmortem Draft'

Create Postmortem Draft action generates a Confluence/Drive skeleton pre-populated with incident metadata, timeline stub, and candidate owners, and adds the link back to the PD incident and Slack thread
Snapshot capture respects PII redaction and configurable retention (default 7 days) and is rate-limited to prevent excessive costs
End-to-end smoke test completes in staging: PD incident -> Slack thread -> generate postmortem -> add a follow-up comment with a PR link
Dashboard widgets show MTTA and MTTR before/after for the service and false-positive rate for auto-created incidents
technical_notes: Architecture: introduce 'escalation-composer' microservice that subscribes to alerts from the rules engine. It calls trace-snapshot API (new endpoint), fetches aggregated metric images (render service), and queries logs via log-pipeline API. It then posts a composed payload to PagerDuty Events API v2 and our Slack ops app. Key constraints: 1) limit snapshot span depth to 100 spans or 2 seconds of trace capture to bound size; 2) redact payloads using current PIIRules lib; 3) sign payloads with service identity for audit; 4) expose toggle per-customer for private deployments.
implementation_steps: Spec escalation-composer API and security model (mutual TLS + service token)
Add trace-snapshot endpoint to tracing-service (implements span depth trim + redaction)
Add rendering endpoint to metric-visualizer to return PNGs for short time windows
Integrate with PagerDuty Events API v2: map severity, service, annotated links
Integrate with Slack Ops app: channel creation, pinned thread, interactive buttons and response handlers
Implement postmortem skeleton generator using templates + user mapping (oncall -> owner), write to Confluence/Drive and return link
Add admin toggles for Private/Dedicated deployments to disable external links where required
Instrument observability for this flow: counters for incidents_created_by_bridge, snapshot_size_bytes, cost_estimate_per_incident
testing_plan: Unit tests for redaction and snapshot size trimming
Integration tests in staging that simulate alert -> full end-to-end flow with synthetic traces and logs
Chaos test: flood alerts and verify rate limiting and graceful degradation (compose a stub payload if services overloaded)
Security review and penetration check on payload signing and storage
Pilot with 2 internal services for 2 weeks, gather MTTA/MTTR metrics and operator feedback
risks: Exfiltration risk if snapshots are not properly redacted - mitigated by PIIRules and review
Cost bloat from high-fidelity snapshots during alert storms - mitigated by trimming and rate limits
On-call noise if too many auto-created incidents - mitigated by threshold tuning and false-positive tracking
rollback_plan: Feature flags: turn off escalation-composer for a region or customer. Remove PD and Slack integrations and fall back to baseline alerting. Retain snapshot storage for audit but stop creation.
